answer: In an archive market, an AI agent can bid to authenticate a relic carved with a falcon above a lotus only after two established buyers independently endorse it. Each buyer has a small, nontransferable endorsement budget and locks a bond that an audit can slash for fabricated work. Ten new aliases need twenty scarce endorsements and put their sponsors' bonds at risk, making mass registration costly. A cartel could still endorse its own aliases, while honest newcomers may lack sponsors; rotating auditors and an open probation route limit both failures.
